requirement: The mdBook preprocessor MUST report an error when a generated requirements index or evidence detail page would use the path of an existing book chapter.
rationale:
structural: The text of `requirements.index.path_conflicts` says: "The mdBook preprocessor MUST report an error when a generated requirements index or evidence detail page would use the path of an existing book chapter." That clause describes observable behavior only. It names a trigger (a generated page's path collides with an existing chapter) and a required outcome (the preprocessor reports an error).

The text names no library, algorithm, signature, type, field or delegation interface. Take an implementation that detects the collision in a different place or with a different data structure, such as a pre-pass over chapters, a set lookup, or a check when inserting each page. It would show the same behavior and still satisfy the text. So how the check is built is discretionary.

No structural obligation needs implementation evidence, so the empty set of review roots is acceptable. Whether the error is actually reported is a behavioral question for the test criterion.

behavioral: The requirement `requirements.index.path_conflicts` has one behavioral obligation. The preprocessor MUST report an error when a generated requirements index or an evidence detail page would use the path of an existing book chapter. It splits into two cases, and each has a test.

1. **Generated index path conflict.** `src/index.rs#mod[tests]/fn[default_index_path_cannot_replace_an_existing_chapter]` is marked `{test}`. It puts an existing chapter at `requirements-index.md`, which is the default generated index path, and has no index marker. It calls `preprocess_book` and asserts an error containing "generated requirements index requirements-index.md conflicts with a book chapter". It also asserts the book is unchanged: one item, with its original content. The error is therefore reported, and the chapter is not replaced.

2. **Detail page conflict.** `src/index.rs#mod[tests]/fn[generated_detail_path_cannot_replace_a_chapter]` is marked `{test}`. It places an existing chapter at `requirements-index/requirements.ready.md`, which is the detail path for `requirements.ready`. It calls `DetailPlan::find` and asserts an `Err` whose message contains "conflicts with a book chapter". It runs both without a `{requirements-index}` marker (default index path) and with a marker chapter at `requirements-index.md`. Because no chapter occupies the index path in either run, the error can only come from the detail-page check.

I read `DetailPlan::find` only to see how the index path is chosen. When a marker chapter exists, the index is that chapter, not a generated page, so only the default-index case can be a generated-index conflict. That case is the one the first test covers. A detail path colliding with an existing chapter is the other case, and the second test covers it in both index modes.

The assertions check both that an error is returned and which conflict it names. They would fail if either conflict were silently accepted. I found no further obligations, boundaries or failure cases the text names that lack a test.
